text: Ghostlight is a passive radar: it never transmits. One antenna records a TV broadcast; a second listens for the faint copies of it that bounce off drones, aircraft and birds.

To stand alone at a substation it needs what the prototype lacks: a mast that survives storms, a sealed box for the electronics, its own power, and enough sensitivity to see a small drone well beyond the fence.

text: 1 of 5 tests pass. Fixing the 4 that don't.

Detection only reaches 0.75 km. The receiver isn't the limit: TV signal leaking into the back of the surveillance antenna raises its noise floor by 44 dB. A bigger antenna wouldn't help, because it would hear the leak just as loudly.
The fix is geometry, not gain: a wire-mesh screen between the antenna and the tower shades it from the direct signal while echoes from the front still get through.

assembly.action: Open the tripod and lock the mast into it
Bolt the surveillance antenna to its arm, facing the area to watch
Hang the mesh screen on the arm, between the surveillance antenna and the TV tower

Mount the SDR and computer in the enclosure and strap it to the mast
Clamp the solar panel to the mast, tilted toward the sun
Set the battery between the tripod legs and connect
